description: Keeps the main thread thin: a clearly multi-step / implementation-shaped Bash by the orchestrator (chained >2 steps, a heredoc, sed -i/tee, npm/cargo/make build, git commit/push, pytest/test runs, AND all `gh` incl. `gh ship`/`gh pr`/`gh run`/`gh api`) warns-then-blocks. A bare >/>> redirect is not implementation on its own. Read-only inspection AND sanctioned orchestration are never blocked, even chained: git status/ls/cat/grep/find, tg, review, git worktree list. ALL `gh` is DELEGATED to a subagent now (Alex tg#7103, reverting the #159/#162 gh-ship carve-out): shipping (`gh ship`) and CI/PR verification (`gh pr checks/view`, `gh run`, `gh api`) are a subagent's job, not inline orchestrator work. Subagent commands (agent_id present) are allowed. WARN first, BLOCK on repeat within ORCH_THIN_TTL_S (900s). Per-repo opt-out (repo owner, not the constrained agent): agent_hooks.orchestrator_only:false in rig.yaml or RIG_ORCHESTRATOR_ONLY=0 (default ON). Deny-by-default: no self-service bypass (ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK env / `# orchestrator-ok:` sentinel removed); a would-be BLOCK consults RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_ORCHESTRATOR_STAYS_THIN with a written justification, which asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl and allows ONLY on an approval tap (a blank/bare 1 denies). timeout_ms 960000 covers tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus margin so a hung/unanswered ask can't race the dispatcher's descriptor-timeout kill into a silent on_error=open ALLOW; a CC settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must set timeout >960s (the 600s CC default would preempt this). on_error=open.
